title: Restriction to a closed support detects the zero action on supported cohomology
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, and twists $A(t)$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary and supported pro-etale cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], the supported cup product [def-pur-supported-cup], and its ordinary pullback and twist identifications [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. For integers $a,b\geq0$ and $t,s\in\mathbf Z$, let $\alpha\in H^a(X,A(t))$ and $\beta\in H^b_Z(X,A(s))$. If $i^*\alpha=0$ in $H^a(Z,A(t))$, then
$$\alpha\cup\beta=0\quad\text{in }H^{a+b}_Z(X,A(t+s)),\qquad \alpha\cup\operatorname{forg}(\beta)=0\quad\text{in }H^{a+b}(X,A(t+s)).$$
Here $\operatorname{forg}$ is the canonical map forgetting support. No smoothness, regularity, Cartier, or purity hypothesis on $X$ or $Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0G75 (remark-support-cup-product), 0G76 (remark-support-cup-product-global), 0G77 (lemma-support-cup-product): closed-support action and forgetting support; the statement is their ordinary finite-coefficient pro-etale analogue, not an application of a ringed-space theorem to a site

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$ and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian. For every affine open $V\subset X$, the open subscheme $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism, by the affine-preimage definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. These are precisely the geometric hypotheses required below for closed pro-etale direct image and its supported essential image.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OZ and topology.tex Tag 04ZA for the open-subscheme consequence

proof.text: Write $S=i_*A_Z$, $F=A_X(t)$, $G=A_X(s)$ and $q:A_X\to S$ for constant restriction. Use [lem-pur-supported-hom] with $i$ and with the identity closed immersion of $X$ to represent the given classes by $\widetilde\alpha:A_X\to F[a]$ and $\widetilde\beta:S\to G[b]$. Both coefficient sheaves are in degree zero, hence bounded below, so this use requires no constructibility or Tor assertion. In [def-pur-supported-cup] the coefficient map for the pair of supports $(X,Z)$ is the left unitor $\lambda_S:A_X\otimes_A^LS\xrightarrow{\sim}S$: its formula is multiplication of constant sections. Consequently the supported product is represented by $\sigma_{a,b}(\widetilde\alpha\otimes\widetilde\beta)\lambda_S^{-1}$, followed by the twist multiplication $F\otimes_A^LG\cong A_X(t+s)$.

source.place: Displayed tensor-morphism definition, with first support X and second support Z; supported Hom is the adjacent lem-pur-supported-hom.md

proof.text: In these representatives forgetting support is precomposition by $q$. Indeed the normalization in [lem-pur-supported-hom-adjunction-transpose] derives the evaluation $v_M(\varphi)=\varphi_X(q(1))$. For a sheaf $M$, inclusion $\Gamma_Z(X,M)\subseteq\Gamma(X,M)$ therefore corresponds to $\varphi\mapsto\varphi q$ under $\operatorname{Hom}(S,M)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,M)=\Gamma(X,M)$. Applying this equality degree by degree on an injective resolution gives the same equality on cohomology. Thus $\operatorname{forg}(\beta)$ is represented by $\widetilde\beta q$; the identical calculation applies to the output coefficient $A_X(t+s)$. The locally Noetherian hypothesis of the normalization lemma follows from Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0G77, lemma-support-cup-product (whose proof is omitted): explicit forgetting-support calculation using the normalized supported-Hom evaluation

proof.text: Ordinary restriction of $\alpha$ is represented by $Li^*\widetilde\alpha:A_Z\to A_Z(t)[a]$. To check the normalization, apply [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] to the full support $X\hookrightarrow X$ and the morphism $i:Z\to X$; its closed-constant exchange is then the coefficient-unit identification. The pro-etale clause applies to the present finite twists: [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] identifies the finite positive Tate twists with the pullbacks of their etale versions, and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] gives those etale twists for every integer. For a negative twist the same comparison follows by dualizing a rank-one locally free sheaf: locally a basis and its dual have evaluation $1$, and the exact comparison inverse image [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], with its tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], preserves this equation, so these dual comparisons glue. Hence the assumption $i^*\alpha=0$ says exactly $Li^*\widetilde\alpha=0$. This uses no comparison for an exceptional inverse image.

source.place: Tag 0G76, remark-support-cup-product-global, first restriction arrow; its pro-etale morphism interpretation uses the cited supported-Hom pullback and finite Tate descent statements

proof.text: The coefficient calculation in [def-pur-supported-cup] proves that $S=i_*A_Z$ is flat. Thus $T:=F[a]\otimes_A^LS$ is the shift $H[a]$ of the sheaf $H:=F\otimes_{A_X}S$: using the degree-zero K-flat model $S$ computes this tensor without a resolution of $F$. By [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint], $j^*S=0$. The underived comparison [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] gives $j^*H\cong j^*F\otimes j^*S=0$. The zero tensor is zero directly from its balanced generators. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image], the actual sheaf adjunction unit $\eta_H:H\to i_*i^*H$ is an isomorphism. Constant coefficient rings satisfy its required inverse-image identifications, as in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact].

Use the derived adjunction $Li^*\dashv i_*$ of [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint]. Here $i_*$ is exact, and $i^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Its unit $\eta_K:K\to i_*Li^*K$ is represented on any complex by the termwise sheaf unit. More explicitly, [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] gives those natural termwise units; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] shows both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and commute with shifts. Localizing the termwise naturality and the two adjunction identities gives this adjunction on the derived categories with these same units. In particular $\eta_T$ is identified with $\eta_H[a]$ under $T\cong H[a]$, and is an isomorphism by Step 5. This is a calculation for a shifted sheaf, not a claim that arbitrary derived morphisms can be checked on their cohomology sheaves.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), termwise computation and shifts; proof of Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives) for the termwise adjunction, localized here for two exact functors

proof.text: Let $m=(\widetilde\alpha\otimes1_S)\lambda_S^{-1}:S\to T$. The finite-level tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] is natural on the ambient pro-etale derived categories, so $Li^*m$ is, up to its invertible unit and tensor comparisons, $(Li^*\widetilde\alpha)\otimes1_{Li^*S}$. This is zero by Step 4. To make preservation of zero explicit, the additive tensor-morphism operation of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus] sends the zero first factor to zero; take its second degree to be zero. Thus $Li^*m=0$.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); the signed additive tensor-morphism calculation is the cited general calculus lemma

proof.text: Naturality of the unit in Step 6 gives $\eta_T\circ m=i_*(Li^*m)\circ\eta_S=0$. Direct image is additive, so it sends the zero morphism of Step 7 to zero. Since $\eta_T$ is invertible, composition with its inverse gives $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G76, factorization through restriction; explicit adjunction-naturality calculation on the pro-etale site

proof.text: Bifunctoriality of derived tensor [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial] gives $\widetilde\alpha\otimes\widetilde\beta=(1_{F[a]}\otimes\widetilde\beta)(\widetilde\alpha\otimes1_S)$. Therefore the morphism representing the supported product in Step 2 equals $\sigma_{a,b}(1_{F[a]}\otimes\widetilde\beta)m$, followed by twist multiplication. It is zero by Step 8. The Hom identification of Step 2 then gives $\alpha\cup\beta=0$ in $H_Z^{a+b}(X,A(t+s))$.

source.place: Displayed tensor-morphism formula; expand tensor bifunctoriality before composing the shift and twist comparisons

proof.text: Finally the unitors satisfy $\lambda_S^{-1}q=(1_{A_X}\otimes q)\lambda_{A_X}^{-1}$, by naturality of $\lambda$. Hence $(\widetilde\alpha\otimes\widetilde\beta)\lambda_S^{-1}q=(\widetilde\alpha\otimes(\widetilde\beta q))\lambda_{A_X}^{-1}$. Composing with the same shift and twist maps proves $\operatorname{forg}(\alpha\cup\beta)=\alpha\cup\operatorname{forg}(\beta)$, using Step 3 for the two forgetful maps and the full-support case of Step 2 for ordinary cup. The left side is zero by Step 9, proving the second assertion.

source.place: Tag 0G77, lemma-support-cup-product: explicit tensor-unitor proof of the omitted compatibility

proof_origin.place: Tags 0G75-0G77 motivate the closed-restriction action and forgetting square; agent proof on ordinary finite-coefficient pro-etale sites using the tensor-morphism definition, closed supported essential image, and natural adjunction unit. No ringed-space result is applied to a site.

lean.statement: theorem closed_supported_cup_vanishing (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {Z X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (a b : ℕ) (t s : ℤ) (α : P.FunctorialCupOrdinaryH true X (a : ℤ) t) (β : P.FunctorialCupH true i (b : ℤ) s) (hα : P.functorialCupOrdinaryPullback true i (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k)) a t α = 0) : P.closedSupportedCup i a b t s α β = 0 ∧ P.closedOrdinaryCup X a b t s α (P.functorialCupForget true i b s β) = 0
lean.note: Both zero conclusions on the actual pro-etale supported-Hom groups. Helpers specialize the published cup using the full-support identity and canonical identity-pullback support identification; ordinary pullback and forgetting support are the recorded functoriality maps.
